quarterly_data.signal: June-quarter mix and operating detail (CFO Doug Bettinger, call): memory 46% of systems revenue, up from 39% in the March quarter and 'a record level for us in total memory' in dollars; non-volatile memory 23%, up from 12%; DRAM 23% versus 27%, flattish in dollars at the March-quarter record; foundry 44%, down from 54% ('Mature node spending with our customers in China was down sequentially. This was largely offset by strength in leading-edge process node investments in 2 and 3 nanometer capability, as well as advanced packaging'); logic and other 10%, up from 7%. Regions: Taiwan 27% (from 23%, 'a new record level for us in dollar terms'), China 26% (from 34%), Korea 20% (from 23%). Operating expenses $916 million versus $866 million, R&D 67% of operating expenses; operating margin 38.4% versus 35%. Days sales outstanding 72 versus 64; inventory $4.3 billion, 'building inventory to meet growing customer demand', turns 3 times versus 2.9 times, 'the highest inventory turns level we've delivered in almost 5 years'; capital expenditures $189 million, 'centered on lab investments in the U.S. and global growth in our manufacturing facilities'.
quarterly_data.figure: Memory 46% (from 39%), foundry 44% (from 54%), logic/other 10%; Taiwan 27%, China 26% (from 34%), Korea 20%; opex $916M; inventory $4.3B, turns 3x; capex $189M

quarterly_data.signal: Customer Support Business Group (call): CFO Doug Bettinger said CSBG revenue of nearly $2.5 billion was up 17% sequentially, 'primarily due to record upgrade revenue', with smaller increases in Reliant and services and spare-part purchases consistent with the strong March level. For September he expects a 'similar profile' - upgrades 'going to continue to be strong ... Driven by what you got going on in NAND investment', spares 'pretty strong given the high utilization in the industry', plus advanced services from cobots and Equipment Intelligence. Beyond 2026: 'We're probably going to do a little bit better than the growth that we talked about a year and a half ago'; Reliant follows mature node investment, China and 'the analog industrial automotive space' - 'That'll be a little bit more situational'.
quarterly_data.figure: CSBG nearly $2.5B, +17% QoQ on record upgrades

quarterly_data.signal: Margins and pricing (call): CFO Doug Bettinger said June-quarter gross margin was stronger 'due to a myriad of factors, including pricing actions, operational and scale efficiencies, as well as a favorable product mix'. Near term: 'we're in that 51%, 52% range right now. I think we can continue to deliver that in the near term.' On the mid-50s gross margin target: 'it's going to take several years, I think, to get to those levels', driven by scale and revenue growth plus 'new product introduction and getting fairly paid for the value we're delivering'. September-quarter spending grows 'albeit at a much slower rate than the growth in revenue'. CEO Tim Archer credited the global manufacturing and supply-chain footprint because 'they're not all interrelated' and Lam can 'get what we need when we need it and also at the prices that we need it'.
quarterly_data.figure: Gross margin 'in that 51%, 52% range' near term; mid-50s target over several years

quarterly_data.signal: Technology wins and advanced packaging (call): CEO Tim Archer said Akara's installed base 'has doubled every year' since launch; Lam's new ALD tools and new etch tools like Akara are 'doing extremely well. Not just in Taiwan, but really at every leading-edge foundry logic customer around the world'. Advanced packaging growth is coming from 'everything ... It's 2.5D. It's in the foundry logic space. It's in HBM', and panel packaging is 'very early stages'; 'just next few years, advanced packaging growth will be a little bit hard to predict because adoption is just occurring all over the place.' CFO Doug Bettinger cited Lam's leadership 'in the TSV etch and the copper electroplating, I call it the drill and fill'. On cleaning, Archer: 'where we are really the focused on the high-performing critical cleans, we've done extremely well.'

Supply chain and capacity investment (call): CFO Doug Bettinger said customer visibility 'is propagating its way all the way back through our supply chain, and even a couple of layers deep'; 'We're doing everything we can to make sure we're not going to be the bottleneck ... We got a lot of things we're expediting'. Capex: 'I still think we can manage the company to 4%-5% of revenue going towards CapEx as we build out lab infrastructure', with a focus on 'footprint densification, getting more output for the same square footage that we have in manufacturing'. CEO Tim Archer: 'Where we see opportunity, we will invest in the company to accelerate growth.' Archer on lead times: 'lead times are challenging', and 'as we move through the second half of the year, that becomes more and more difficult to see anything further in this year as true surprise upside'.
